doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Leaving Washington with Earl Bostic's band
summary: Cobb says Keter Betts got him the Earl Bostic job at 21, his way out of Washington to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Tell us one of the gigs that you were on when you in your own mind said I’ve arrived — I’m a player, I’m on the scene and I have a voice here.

Well I think that must have been when Keter Betts got me a job with Earl Bostic’s band and I left town. I didn’t say I’ve arrived, I say I’m leaving. Which is, so I left, from my standpoint, I’m leaving. But you know that was a pretty good thing because I didn’t know if I was ever going to get out of the town. I got to be 21 years old and I got to leave so it was great. I went to New York and then from New York I stayed in New York, which © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

that was my passage out of Washington. Not that I didn’t love Washington, I still love it. But it’s not like you’re going to make a living around there playing music. Maybe some people do but I didn’t think I could. I figured New York was the place for me. And it turned out. It worked out.
